questions.q: What is a baby cat called?
questions.fact: Kittens are born with their eyes closed and open them after about one to two weeks.

questions.q: What is a baby goat called?
questions.fact: Baby goats can stand and walk within minutes of being born.

questions.q: What is a baby horse called?
questions.fact: A young female horse is called a filly and a young male is called a colt.

questions.q: What is a baby swan called?
questions.fact: Cygnets are usually gray or brown, not white like their parents.

questions.q: What is a baby goose called?
questions.fact: Goslings can swim within a day or so of hatching.

questions.q: What is a baby owl called?
questions.fact: Owlets are covered in fluffy down feathers before their adult feathers grow in.

questions.q: What is a baby deer called?
questions.fact: Many fawns have white spots that help them hide in dappled forest light.

questions.q: What is a baby bear called?
questions.fact: Black bear cubs are about the size of a squirrel when they are born.

questions.q: What is a baby whale called?
questions.fact: A newborn blue whale calf can weigh more than 2,500 kilograms.

questions.q: What is a baby fox called?
questions.fact: Fox kits are born in an underground den.

questions.q: What is a baby seal called?
questions.fact: Some seal pups are born with fluffy white fur.

questions.q: What is a baby eel called?
questions.fact: Young eels are see-through when they are small and are called glass eels.

questions.q: What is a group of crows called?
questions.fact: Crows are very smart and can recognize individual human faces.

questions.q: What is a group of owls called?
questions.fact: The name may come from an old story that described owls as wise.

questions.q: What is a group of whales or dolphins called?
questions.fact: Some dolphin pods join together to make superpods of more than a thousand animals.

questions.q: What is a group of fish swimming together called?
questions.fact: Swimming in a school helps fish confuse predators.

questions.q: What is a group of wolves called?
questions.fact: A wolf pack is usually a family made of parents and their young.

questions.q: What is a group of geese on the ground called?
questions.fact: Flying geese in a V shape are often called a skein.

questions.q: What is a group of monkeys called?
questions.fact: Some monkey troops have more than a hundred members.

questions.q: What is a group of flamingos called?
questions.fact: Flamingos often stand on one leg, even while sleeping.

questions.q: What is a group of ants called?
questions.fact: Some ant colonies have millions of ants working together.

questions.q: What is a group of cows called?
questions.fact: Cows in a herd often have best friends and get stressed when separated.

questions.q: What is the fastest bird in a dive?
questions.fact: A diving peregrine falcon can go faster than 320 kilometers per hour.

questions.q: What is the fastest fish in the sea?
questions.fact: Sailfish are often said to reach speeds of over 100 kilometers per hour in short bursts.

questions.q: Which is the largest living land animal?
questions.fact: A big male African elephant can weigh about 6,000 kilograms or more.

questions.q: Which animal has the longest pregnancy of any mammal?
questions.fact: An elephant mother is pregnant for about 22 months.

questions.q: What is an elephant's trunk?
choices: Its nose joined with its upper lip
questions.fact: An elephant's trunk has tens of thousands of muscles.

questions.q: What are an elephant's tusks?
questions.fact: Elephant tusks are made of ivory and keep growing all their lives.

questions.q: How can you tell an African elephant from an Asian elephant?
choices: African elephants have much bigger ears
questions.fact: An African elephant's big ears are shaped a bit like the continent of Africa.

questions.q: Why do elephants flap their big ears?
questions.fact: Blood flowing through their thin ears loses heat when the ears flap.

questions.q: Which animal is the largest living cat?
questions.fact: Siberian tigers, also called Amur tigers, are the biggest of all.

questions.q: Which big cat lives in groups called prides?
questions.fact: Lions are the only truly social big cats.

questions.q: In a lion pride, who does most of the hunting?
questions.fact: Lionesses often hunt together as a team.

questions.q: Which big cat is a great swimmer and often hunts in water?
questions.fact: Unlike most cats, tigers usually enjoy water.

questions.q: What are a tiger's stripes like?
choices: All tigers have the same pattern
Stripes are only on the fur, not the skin
Tigers have spots under their stripes
questions.fact: A tiger's skin is striped too, not just its fur.

questions.q: Which big cat lives high in the mountains of Central Asia?
questions.fact: Snow leopards use their long, thick tails like a scarf to keep warm.

questions.q: Which big cat lives mostly in Central and South America?
questions.fact: Jaguars have one of the strongest bites of all big cats.

questions.q: How can you tell a jaguar's spots from a leopard's?
choices: Jaguar spots often have small dots inside
questions.fact: The rings of spots on both cats are called rosettes.

questions.q: Which cat cannot roar but can purr?
questions.fact: Cheetahs chirp, purr and even make bird-like calls.

questions.q: Why do cheetahs have black lines running from their eyes?
choices: They are tear stains from crying
They help cut down glare from the sun
questions.fact: These tear marks may work like the black grease that some athletes wear under their eyes.

questions.q: What is the largest member of the dog family?
questions.fact: Gray wolves can weigh more than 60 kilograms.

questions.q: Which wild dog lives in Australia?
questions.fact: Dingoes have lived in Australia for thousands of years.

questions.q: Which animal is known for laughing sounds?
questions.fact: The giggle-like sounds help hyenas tell each other who is around and how they feel.

questions.q: What is a zebra's skin color underneath its stripes?
questions.fact: Scientists think the stripes may help keep biting flies away.

questions.q: Which large flightless bird lives only in Australia?
questions.fact: Emus are the second tallest birds in the world after ostriches.

questions.q: Which bird lays the largest eggs?
questions.fact: An ostrich egg weighs about as much as two dozen chicken eggs.

questions.q: Which country is the kiwi bird from?
questions.fact: The kiwi cannot fly and has nostrils at the tip of its long beak.

questions.q: Which bird can turn its head about three quarters of the way around?
questions.fact: Owls cannot move their eyes, so they turn their heads instead.

questions.q: Which bird is the national bird of the United States?
questions.fact: Bald eagles are not actually bald, their heads are covered in white feathers.

questions.q: What do bald eagles mainly eat?
questions.fact: Bald eagles sometimes steal fish from other birds, like ospreys.

questions.q: What makes flamingos pink?
questions.fact: Flamingos eat tiny shrimp and algae full of pink color, and without it their feathers turn pale.

questions.q: Which bird is famous for copying human speech?
questions.fact: An African gray parrot named Alex learned more than 100 words.

questions.q: Which bird has the longest wingspan of any living bird?
questions.fact: A wandering albatross can have wings over 3 meters from tip to tip.

questions.q: Which bird is the smallest in the world?
questions.fact: The bee hummingbird from Cuba is only about 5 centimeters long.

questions.q: How fast can a hummingbird's wings beat?
questions.fact: Some small hummingbirds beat their wings around 80 times a second.

questions.q: Which bird has a huge, colorful bill and lives in South American rainforests?
questions.fact: A toucan's bill looks heavy but is light, made of a spongy material.

questions.q: Which bird can hold lots of fish in a stretchy pouch under its bill?
questions.fact: A brown pelican dives headfirst into the water to catch fish.

questions.q: Which seabird with a colorful beak is sometimes called a sea parrot?
questions.fact: Puffins can carry many small fish in their beaks at once.

questions.q: Which bird is famous for its huge, colorful tail feathers?
questions.fact: Only the males, called peacocks, have the big fancy tails, and the females are called peahens.

questions.q: Where do most penguins live?
questions.fact: No penguins live in the wild at the North Pole.

questions.q: Which is the largest kind of penguin?
questions.fact: Emperor penguins can stand more than 1 meter tall.

questions.q: Which parent keeps an emperor penguin egg warm through the Antarctic winter?
questions.fact: The father balances the egg on his feet under a warm fold of skin for about two months.

questions.q: What is the smallest kind of penguin?
questions.fact: Little penguins, also called fairy penguins, are only about 33 centimeters tall.

questions.q: Which bird builds the biggest nests?
questions.fact: One bald eagle nest in Florida was estimated to weigh more than 2 tons.

questions.q: Which bird can stay in the air for about 10 months without landing?
questions.fact: Common swifts even eat and drink while flying.

questions.q: Which bird migrates the farthest each year?
questions.fact: Arctic terns fly from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back every year.

questions.q: What do we call it when birds lose old feathers and grow new ones?
questions.fact: Most birds molt at least once a year.

questions.q: Which bird uses tools like twigs to pull insects out of holes?
questions.fact: These crows even bend and shape their tools.

questions.q: Which bird pecks holes in trees to find insects?
questions.fact: Woodpeckers can peck around 20 times every second.

questions.q: Which bird is a symbol of peace?
questions.fact: Doves and pigeons belong to the same bird family.

questions.q: Which bird hoots and hunts mostly at night?
questions.fact: Owls have special soft feathers that let them fly almost silently.

questions.q: Which mammal lays eggs and has a bill like a duck?
questions.fact: Platypuses use their bills to sense tiny electric signals from prey underwater.

questions.q: Besides the platypus, which other mammal lays eggs?
questions.fact: Egg-laying mammals are called monotremes.

questions.q: Where does a mother kangaroo carry her baby?
questions.fact: Animals with pouches are called marsupials.

questions.q: Which animal from Australia sleeps up to 20 hours a day and eats eucalyptus leaves?
questions.fact: Eucalyptus leaves give koalas little energy, so they rest a lot.

questions.q: Is a koala a bear?
questions.fact: Koala babies, like kangaroo babies, are called joeys.

questions.q: Which Australian animal makes poop shaped like cubes?
questions.fact: Wombats leave their cube-shaped poop on rocks and logs to mark their territory.

questions.q: Which marsupial from Tasmania is known for its loud screeches?
questions.fact: Tasmanian devils have one of the strongest bites for their size of any mammal.

questions.q: Which small Australian marsupial is famous for looking like it is smiling?
questions.fact: Quokkas live mostly on Rottnest Island near Perth.

questions.q: Which is the only marsupial native to the United States and Canada?
questions.fact: When scared, an opossum may play dead, flopping over and lying very still.

questions.q: Which animal sprays a bad smell to defend itself?
questions.fact: A skunk can spray its smelly liquid about 3 meters.

questions.q: Which animal has a hard shell made of bony plates and can sometimes roll into a ball?
questions.fact: Only the three-banded armadillo can roll into a complete ball.

questions.q: Which animal is covered in sharp quills?
questions.fact: Porcupines cannot shoot their quills, but the quills come off easily when touched.

questions.q: Which animal builds dams across streams?
questions.fact: Beavers' front teeth never stop growing, and they are orange because of iron.

questions.q: Which animal holds hands with others while sleeping so they don't drift apart?
questions.fact: Sea otters also wrap themselves in seaweed to stay in place.

questions.q: Which animal uses rocks as tools to crack open shellfish?
questions.fact: Sea otters even keep a favorite rock in a pouch of skin under their arm.

questions.q: Which animal has long tusks and uses them to pull itself onto ice?
questions.fact: Both male and female walruses have tusks.

questions.q: Which whale has a long spiral tusk that makes it look like a unicorn?
questions.fact: A narwhal's tusk is actually a long tooth that grows through its lip.

questions.q: Which white whale is known as the canary of the sea for its many sounds?
questions.fact: Belugas can change the shape of their bumpy forehead, called a melon.

questions.q: Which whale is famous for its long, beautiful songs?
questions.fact: Male humpbacks sing songs that can last for hours.

questions.q: What is another name for the orca?
questions.fact: Orcas are actually the largest members of the dolphin family.

questions.q: Which whale has the largest brain of any animal?
questions.fact: A sperm whale's brain weighs about 8 kilograms.

questions.q: How do whales breathe?
choices: Through a blowhole on top of their head
questions.fact: The spout you see is warm breath and water spray from the blowhole.

questions.q: What do blue whales mainly eat?
questions.fact: A blue whale can eat several tons of these tiny shrimp-like animals in a day.

questions.q: What do some whales have in their mouths instead of teeth, to strain food from water?
questions.fact: Baleen is made of keratin, the same stuff as your fingernails.

questions.q: How do dolphins find food using sound?
choices: Seeing in the dark with night vision
questions.fact: Dolphins send out clicks and listen for the echoes bouncing back.

questions.q: How do dolphins sleep?
choices: With both eyes closed for 12 hours
With half of their brain at a time
questions.fact: Keeping half the brain awake lets them keep breathing and watch for danger.

questions.q: Which sea mammal is also called a sea cow?
questions.fact: Manatees are plant eaters and their closest land relatives are elephants.

questions.q: How can you tell a sea lion from a true seal?
choices: Seals can walk on all four flippers
questions.fact: Sea lions can also turn their back flippers forward to walk on land.

questions.q: Which shark is the largest predator fish?
questions.fact: The whale shark is bigger, but it eats tiny plankton instead of hunting big prey.

questions.q: What are shark skeletons made of?
questions.fact: Cartilage is the same bendy material in your nose and ears.

questions.q: How many rows of teeth can a shark have?
choices: Many rows, replaced all through its life
Only one row that never changes
questions.fact: Some sharks lose and replace thousands of teeth in their lifetime.

questions.q: Which shark has a head shaped like a wide flat hammer?
questions.fact: The wide head spreads out the eyes and sensors, helping it find prey.

questions.q: Which shark can swim from the ocean far up into fresh water rivers?
questions.fact: Bull sharks have been found far up the Mississippi and Amazon rivers.

questions.q: Which shark lives the longest, possibly hundreds of years?
questions.fact: Scientists estimate that some Greenland sharks may live 270 years or more.

questions.q: Which fish can puff up into a spiky ball?
questions.fact: Many pufferfish contain a strong poison, so most predators leave them alone.

questions.q: Which fish lives safely among the stinging tentacles of sea anemones?
questions.fact: A slimy coating protects clownfish from the anemone's stings.

questions.q: Which fish swims from the ocean back up the river where it hatched to lay eggs?
questions.fact: Salmon may use their sense of smell to find their home stream.

questions.q: Which fish has a glowing lure on its head to attract prey in the deep sea?
questions.fact: The glow comes from bacteria living in the lure.

questions.q: Which fish has both eyes on one side of its head and lies flat on the sea floor?
questions.fact: Baby flounders start with eyes on both sides, and one eye moves over as they grow.

questions.q: In which fish species does the male give birth?
questions.fact: The female puts her eggs into a pouch on the male's belly, and he carries them until they hatch.

questions.q: Which fish can make strong electric shocks?
questions.fact: Despite its name, the electric eel is actually a type of knifefish.

questions.q: Which fish is known for its sharp teeth and lives in South American rivers?
questions.fact: Most piranhas eat a mix of food, including seeds and fruit, and rarely attack people.

questions.q: What do fish use to breathe underwater?
questions.fact: Gills pull oxygen out of the water as it flows over them.

questions.q: Which ocean animal shoots out ink to escape from predators?
questions.fact: The ink cloud confuses predators while the octopus swims away.

questions.q: What color is an octopus's blood?
questions.fact: Octopus blood uses copper to carry oxygen, which makes it blue.

questions.q: How many arms does an octopus have?
questions.fact: Each arm has its own cluster of nerves and can taste what it touches.

questions.q: Which animal can change both the color and texture of its skin in less than a second?
questions.fact: Octopuses have special color cells in their skin that they control with muscles.

questions.q: Which animal has the largest eyes of any animal?
questions.fact: A colossal squid's eye can be about the size of a soccer ball.

questions.q: How many arms does a typical sea star have?
questions.fact: Some sea stars can regrow a lost arm, and a few kinds have many more arms.

questions.q: Is a sea star a fish?
questions.fact: Sea stars have no blood and move water through their bodies instead.

questions.q: Which ocean animal is actually a colony of many tiny animals living together?
questions.fact: Each part of a man o' war is a separate tiny creature, and they cannot live alone.

questions.q: What is a coral reef made from?
choices: Skeletons of tiny animals called coral polyps
questions.fact: Coral reefs cover a tiny part of the ocean floor but are home to about a quarter of all ocean species.

questions.q: Which animal is a hermit crab known for using as a home?
questions.fact: Hermit crabs move into bigger shells as they grow.

questions.q: How many legs does a crab have?
questions.fact: Two of the crab's ten legs are its front claws, called pincers.

questions.q: Which sea turtle is the largest?
questions.fact: Leatherbacks can weigh more than 500 kilograms.

questions.q: Where do sea turtles lay their eggs?
choices: In nests dug on sandy beaches
questions.fact: Many females return to lay eggs on the same beach where they hatched.

questions.q: What decides whether many baby sea turtles hatch as males or females?
questions.fact: Warmer nests mostly produce females and cooler nests mostly produce males.

questions.q: Which reptile can live for more than 150 years?
questions.fact: A giant tortoise named Jonathan, living on the island of Saint Helena, was over 190 years old as of 2025.

questions.q: What is the difference between a tortoise and a turtle?
choices: Tortoises live on land, while many turtles live in water
questions.fact: Tortoises usually have rounded, dome-shaped shells and stumpy legs.

questions.q: Which reptile is the largest living reptile?
questions.fact: Big male saltwater crocodiles can grow longer than 6 meters.

questions.q: How can you tell a crocodile from an alligator?
choices: Crocodiles usually have a narrower, pointed snout
questions.fact: When a crocodile closes its mouth, you can usually still see some of its lower teeth.

questions.q: In which two countries do wild alligators live?
questions.fact: The Chinese alligator is much smaller and is critically endangered.

questions.q: Which lizard can change color and move its eyes in two directions at once?
questions.fact: A chameleon's tongue can be longer than its whole body.

questions.q: Which lizard can walk up walls and even across ceilings?
questions.fact: Geckos have millions of tiny hairs on their toes that stick to surfaces.

questions.q: Which lizard can squirt blood from its eyes to scare away predators?
questions.fact: The blood tastes bad to predators like dogs and coyotes.

questions.q: Why do some lizards drop their tails?
questions.fact: The tail keeps wiggling to distract the predator, and a new tail can grow back.

questions.q: Which venomous lizard lives in the deserts of the southwestern United States and Mexico?
questions.fact: Gila monsters spend most of their lives underground.

questions.q: Which is the longest snake in the world?
questions.fact: Reticulated pythons can grow longer than 6 meters.

questions.q: Which is the heaviest snake in the world?
questions.fact: Green anacondas can weigh more than 90 kilograms, about as much as a grown-up.

questions.q: Which is the longest venomous snake?
questions.fact: King cobras can be more than 5 meters long and mostly eat other snakes.

questions.q: How do snakes smell?
questions.fact: A snake flicks its tongue to collect smells and then presses it to a special organ in its mouth.

questions.q: What does a rattlesnake use its rattle for?
choices: To warn animals to stay away
questions.fact: A new segment is added to the rattle each time the snake sheds its skin.

questions.q: How do snakes grow?
questions.fact: Snakes often shed their skin in one long piece, inside out.

questions.q: How do snakes like pythons and boas kill their prey?
questions.fact: Snakes that squeeze their prey are called constrictors.

questions.q: Do snakes have eyelids?
questions.fact: Instead, a clear scale covers and protects each eye.

questions.q: What are the only animals that have feathers?
questions.fact: Some dinosaurs had feathers too, and birds are their living relatives.

questions.q: Which amphibian can regrow lost legs, and even parts of its heart and brain?
questions.fact: Axolotls are a kind of salamander from lakes near Mexico City.

questions.q: How do frogs drink water?
choices: They soak it up through their skin
questions.fact: Many frogs have a special patch of skin on their belly for soaking up water.

questions.q: What is the difference between a frog and a toad?
choices: Toads usually have dry, bumpy skin and shorter legs
questions.fact: All toads are actually a type of frog.

questions.q: Which brightly colored frog from rainforests has poisonous skin?
questions.fact: Some Indigenous people used the poison on the tips of their blow darts.

questions.q: What does the word amphibian mean?
questions.fact: Most amphibians start life in water and later live partly on land.

questions.q: Which animal group are frogs, toads and salamanders part of?
questions.fact: Amphibians have thin skin that must stay moist.

questions.q: How many legs do insects have?
questions.fact: Insects also have three main body parts: head, thorax and abdomen.

questions.q: Which group of animals do spiders belong to?
questions.fact: Scorpions, ticks and mites are arachnids too.

questions.q: What is the name for an animal with no backbone?
questions.fact: About 97 percent of all animal species are invertebrates.

questions.q: What do caterpillars turn into inside a chrysalis to become butterflies?
choices: They grow wings on the outside first
questions.fact: This complete change of body shape is called metamorphosis.

questions.q: Which butterfly travels thousands of kilometers from Canada to Mexico every year?
questions.fact: Millions of monarchs spend the winter clustered on trees in the mountains of Mexico.

questions.q: What do butterflies taste with?
questions.fact: Butterflies stand on a leaf to taste whether it is good for laying eggs.

questions.q: Which insect makes honey?
questions.fact: A single honeybee makes only about one twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its whole life.

questions.q: Who is the only bee in a hive that lays eggs?
questions.fact: A queen bee can lay up to about 2,000 eggs in a single day.

questions.q: What are male honeybees called?
questions.fact: Drones do not have stingers.

questions.q: What happens to a honeybee after it stings a person?
questions.fact: The barbed stinger gets stuck in skin and tears away from the bee.

questions.q: Which insects make light to attract mates?
questions.fact: The light from fireflies makes almost no heat.

questions.q: How do crickets make their chirping sound?
questions.fact: You can roughly estimate the temperature by counting cricket chirps.

questions.q: Which insect is famous for carrying many times its own body weight?
questions.fact: Some ants can lift around 50 times their own weight.

questions.q: Which insect is known for spending years underground and then all coming out together to sing loudly?
questions.fact: Some periodical cicadas stay underground for 17 years.

questions.q: Which insect only drinks blood when it is a female?
questions.fact: Female mosquitoes need protein from blood to make their eggs, while males drink plant nectar.

questions.q: Which animal kills more people each year than any other wild animal?
questions.fact: Mosquitoes spread diseases like malaria.

questions.q: Which insect has been around since before the dinosaurs and can hunt other insects in mid-air?
questions.fact: Dragonflies catch a very high share of the prey they chase.

questions.q: Which beetle is red with black spots and eats aphids?
questions.fact: One ladybug can eat thousands of aphids during its life.

questions.q: Which insect can hide by looking just like a twig?
questions.fact: Some stick insects are longer than a ruler.

questions.q: What do dung beetles do with animal poop?
choices: Roll it into balls and eat it or lay eggs in it
questions.fact: Some dung beetles use the Milky Way in the night sky to find their way.

questions.q: Which insect group has the most species on Earth?
questions.fact: Scientists have described about 400,000 kinds of beetles.

questions.q: What do termites mainly eat?
questions.fact: Some African termites build mounds taller than a grown-up.

questions.q: What is the young of a dragonfly that lives underwater called?
questions.fact: A dragonfly nymph can spend years underwater before becoming a flying adult.

questions.q: How does a spider catch most of its food?
choices: In silk webs or by hunting
questions.fact: Weight for weight, spider silk can be stronger than steel.

questions.q: Which spider is famous for eating its mate?
questions.fact: Female black widows do sometimes eat males, but not every time.

questions.q: Which spider is large and hairy and sometimes kept as a pet?
questions.fact: Some tarantulas can live for more than 20 years.

questions.q: Which spider mother carries her babies on her back?
questions.fact: Hundreds of tiny spiderlings may ride on their mother's back.

questions.q: Which ape is the closest living relative of humans, along with the bonobo?
questions.fact: Humans and chimpanzees share about 98 percent of their DNA.

questions.q: Which is the largest ape?
questions.fact: A big male gorilla, called a silverback, can weigh more than 180 kilograms.

questions.q: Which ape has reddish-orange hair and lives in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra?
questions.fact: Orangutan means person of the forest in the Malay language.

questions.q: Which apes swing through the trees with super long arms and sing loud songs?
questions.fact: Gibbons can swing between branches at up to about 55 kilometers per hour.

questions.q: Which scientist became famous for studying wild chimpanzees in Tanzania?
questions.fact: Jane Goodall discovered that chimpanzees make and use tools.

questions.q: Where do wild lemurs live?
questions.fact: Lemurs live naturally only on the island of Madagascar and a few small nearby islands.

questions.q: What is the difference between a monkey and an ape?
choices: Apes have tails and monkeys do not
Most monkeys have tails and apes do not
questions.fact: Gorillas, chimpanzees, orangutans and gibbons are all apes.

questions.q: Which monkey is known as one of the loudest land animals?
questions.fact: A howler monkey's call can be heard several kilometers away through the forest.

questions.q: Which monkey lives in snowy mountains in Japan and bathes in hot springs?
questions.fact: These monkeys are often called snow monkeys.

questions.q: Which monkey has a bright red and blue face?
questions.fact: Mandrills are the largest monkeys in the world.

questions.q: What is the largest rodent in the world?
questions.fact: Capybaras live in South America and love to swim.

questions.q: Which rodent stores food in big cheek pouches?
questions.fact: A hamster can stuff its cheek pouches until its head looks twice as wide.

questions.q: Is a rabbit a rodent?
choices: It is a type of cat
questions.fact: Rabbits have a second small pair of upper front teeth behind the first pair.

questions.q: Which pet rodent comes from South America and makes squeaking sounds called wheeking?
questions.fact: Guinea pigs are not pigs and do not come from Guinea.

questions.q: Which animal has the softest, thickest fur of any land animal?
questions.fact: A chinchilla can grow about 60 hairs from a single hair follicle.

questions.q: Which small mammal digs tunnels and is almost blind?
questions.fact: A mole can dig about 18 meters of tunnel in a day.

questions.q: Which African rodent has almost no hair and lives in colonies with a queen, like bees?
questions.fact: Naked mole-rats can live more than 30 years, a very long time for a rodent.

questions.q: How do most bats find insects in the dark?
questions.fact: Bats send out high-pitched calls and listen for the echoes.

questions.q: What do vampire bats drink?
questions.fact: Vampire bats share blood meals with roost mates who did not find food.

questions.q: Which bat is the largest, with wings over 1.5 meters wide?
questions.fact: Flying foxes eat fruit and nectar, not insects.
